title: Stepwise Tfh cell differentiation revisited: new advances and long-standing questions
summary: Review framing Tfh differentiation as a multi-step process in which activated CD4+ T cells upregulate CXCR5 as CXCR5+ precursor Tfh (pre-Tfh) cells, a subset of which enter B-cell follicles to become GC-Tfh while others take a different (memory) fate. Supports the identity of the atlas 'preT follicular helper' label as the pre-Tfh intermediate. Markers here (CXCR5) are discussed as transcript/receptor expression.
quotes: it is still not fully understood how a subset of activated CD4+ T cells begin to express CXCR5 during the early stage of the response and, shortly after, how some CXCR5+ precursor Tfh (pre-Tfh) cells enter B cell follicles and differentiate further into germinal center Tfh (GC-Tfh) cells while others have a different fate

title: Follicular helper T cells (Tfh): heterogeneity in spatial distribution and phenotypic characteristics
summary: Describes Tfh fate as primed at the T:B border of secondary lymphoid organs, with BCL6-driven commitment. Newly committed pre-Tfh upregulate CXCR5 and downregulate CCR7, then migrate along a CXCL13 gradient into the follicle. This directly supports the location (T:B border / follicle) and the CXCR5-intermediate/CCR7+ transitional phenotype of the atlas cell type. CXCR5, CCR7 and EBI2 discussed as chemokine receptors (protein/transcript).
quotes: Tfh cell fate is primed at the T-B border of secondary lymphoid organs.

Upon upregulating CXCR5 and downregulating the T-zone homing receptor CCR7, newly committed pre-Tfh cells migrate towards the CXCL13 chemokine gradient into the follicle and mature into GC-Tfh (14-16). The initial positioning of pre-Tfh within GC is regulated by a balance of CXCR5, CCR7, and EBI2 signaling (17).

title: Advances and challenges in identifying precursors of memory CD4+ T cells
summary: Reviews the spatial/receptor logic connecting pre-Tfh to memory. CXCR5 positions pre-Tfh at the T:B border and enables follicle entry; PD-1 upregulation promotes GC-territory accumulation; CCR7 retains cells in the T-cell zone and inhibits Tfh differentiation even when CXCR5 is co-expressed. This underpins the 'central-memory-phenotype pre-Tfh' interpretation: a CXCR5+CCR7+ cell poised between T-zone retention and follicular commitment. Receptors discussed at expression/positioning level (protein).
quotes: Expression of CXCR5, which facilitates positioning of pre-Tfh cells at T:B border and entry into follicle to appropriately interact with B cells, is essential for further GC-Tfh and Tfh memory cell differentiation
CCR7 expression retains activated CD4 + T cells in T cell zone and thus inhibits their differentiation towards Tfh fate, despite co-expression of CXCR5

title: Spatiotemporal resolution of germinal center Tfh cell differentiation and divergence from central memory CD4+ T cell fate
summary: Directly addresses the fate bifurcation implied by the atlas label 'central memory ... preT follicular helper'. PD-1+CXCR5+ pre-Tfh cells either transition to GC-Tfh (marked by sustained Tigit) or upregulate IL-7Ra to become CXCR5+ memory CD4+ T cells with or without CCR7 — i.e. a central-memory-like fate. Markers cited here are transcript/chromatin-level (PD-1, CXCR5, Bcl6, Tigit, IL-7Ra) from mouse single-cell/ATAC data.
quotes: the sustained Tigit expression in PD-1+CXCR5+CD4+ T cells marks the precursor Tfh (pre-Tfh) to GC-Tfh transition, whereas Tigit–PD-1+CXCR5+CD4+ T cells upregulate IL-7Rα to become CXCR5+CD4+ T memory cells with or without CCR7
our work identifies an important marker and regulatory mechanism of PD-1+CXCR5+CD4+ T cells during their developmental choice between memory T cell fate and GC-Tfh cell differentiation

title: Neonatal T Follicular Helper Cells Are Lodged in a Pre-T Follicular Helper Stage Favoring Innate Over Adaptive Germinal Center Responses
summary: Characterises the pre-Tfh stage as a distinct, incompletely-committed developmental state defined by a multi-signal program (CXCR5, IL-21, Bcl6, Ascl2, c-maf). Ascl2 drives CXCR5 and suppresses CCR7 to control follicular localisation; CXCR5 enables migration into follicles and stable B-cell contacts. Supports marker set and the transitional nature of the atlas cell type. Markers here are gene-expression (transcript) measurements.
quotes: T fh cells differentiation involves a multisignal process that includes expression of CXCR5, IL-21, Bcl6, TBK1, STAT4, Ascl2, and c-maf
Ascl2 directly regulates the localization of T fh cells via CXCR5 expression and suppression of CCR7 and PSGL1

title: Cxc Chemokine Receptor 5 Expression Defines Follicular Homing T Cells with B Cell Helper Function
summary: Foundational tonsil study showing that essentially all CD4+ memory T cells in human tonsil are CXCR5+ and express activation markers (CD69, HLA-DR, ICOS), with strong downregulation of CCR7 and CD62L, consistent with recent tissue entry and follicular homing. Directly relevant to the adult palatine-tonsil context and the CXCR5/CCR7 receptor logic of the atlas cell type. Markers measured at cell-surface (protein) level.
quotes: Practically all (Ͼ95%) CD4 ϩ memory T cells in tonsils are CXCR5 ϩ and the majority express activation markers (CD69, HLA-DR, ICOS) suggesting their engagement in B cell activation. Drastic reduction in cell surface CCR7 and CD62L indicates that the majority of local CXCR5 ϩ T cells have recently entered the tonsillar tissue

title: Memory T Follicular Helper CD4 T Cells
summary: Reviews the memory Tfh concept and the distinction between activated tonsillar CXCR5+CD4+ T cells (CD69+HLA-DR+ICOS+) and resting circulating CXCR5+ cells (CD69-HLA-DR-ICOS-) proposed to be memory Tfh. Supports the 'central-memory-phenotype' component of the atlas label. Activation markers here are cell-surface (protein) phenotypes.
quotes: unlike the activated tonsillar CXCR5+ CD4 T cells that were CD69+HLA-DR+ICOS+, circulating CXCR5+ cells in human blood are CD69−HLA-DR− ICOS−, and hypothesized that these blood CXCR5+ cells represent memory Tfh cells

title: Germinal center B cell and T follicular helper cell development initiates in the inter-follicular zone
summary: Shows that Tfh differentiation initiates in the interfollicular/T:B border zone, where responding T cells upregulate Bcl6 and acquire CXCR5, PD-1 and GL7 before migrating into the follicle; the full PD-1hi ICOShi GL7hi GC-Tfh phenotype requires cognate B cells. Grounds the location (T:B border) and the pre-Tfh-to-GC-Tfh maturation gradient (PD-1, ICOS as maturation markers). Markers are protein-level (flow/immunofluorescence).
quotes: T cells also acquired the Tfh cell markers CXCR5, PD-1 and GL7.
Ag-specific B cells are required for the maintenance of the PD-1hi ICOShi GL7hi Tfh cell phenotype within the follicle, but not for their initial differentiation in the IF zone.

title: CD4+ T follicular helper (Tfh) cells in human tonsil and blood are clonally convergent, but divergent from non-Tfh CD4+ cells
summary: Donor-matched TCR-repertoire study of human tonsil and blood showing clonal convergence between tonsillar GC-Tfh, tonsillar CXCR3- Tfh and blood CXCR5+PD-1+ circulating Tfh, consistent with a shared precursor relationship. Relevant to the adult tonsil context and the idea that pre-Tfh/central-memory Tfh precursors interconnect tissue and circulation. Markers (CXCR5, PD-1, CXCR3) are surface-protein sorting phenotypes.
quotes: our analysis of donormatched tissues directly demonstrates that the same Tfh clones are present in both tonsil and the blood CXCR5 + PD-1 + cTfh compartment
